name: Dusk Grove
summary: Modern HD-2D pixel art: an enchanted forest clearing at golden-to-violet dusk, rim-lit sprites, banded glows, bloom and long shadows.
description: Low-resolution pixel art (1 world unit = 1 art pixel, nearest-neighbour upscaled) that is lit like a modern 3D scene. Every sprite is shaded per pixel from a light vector, gets a warm sun rim on its left/top edges, a cool violet bounce on the right and a selective outline tinted from its own colours. Emissive faces, mushrooms and lanterns throw additive banded glows, shadows are sheared long towards the upper right, and the whole low-res buffer is colour-graded peach-to-violet with soft bloom and a violet vignette. It feels magical, warm and slightly melancholic: the last golden minute before night.
bestFor: farming/forest games with a day-night cycle
avoidFor: projects that need flat, icon-like readability at tiny sizes
very fast bullet-hell scenes with hundreds of sprites

difficulty.why: The most detailed pixel style: every new asset has to be painted pixel by pixel from shaded primitives into hue-shifted ramps, then get the two-tone rim, the tinted selective outline, a sheared shadow, often an emissive glow and both facings – keeping new assets consistent at this level of quality is a lot of work.

technique.resolution: Low-res buffer with 360 art pixels of height (1 world unit = 1 art pixel), upscaled by an integer factor (round(displayHeight/360)) with imageSmoothingEnabled = false. Sprites are painted pixel by pixel into RGBA buffers and baked once.
technique.summary: Sprites are built from shaded ellipsoids/cylinders whose N·L value indexes a hand-picked, hue-shifted colour ramp; a finishing pass adds a two-tone rim light and a selective outline. Post-processing (multiply tint, bloom, sun glow, vignette, tilt-shift) runs on the low-res buffer before upscaling, so even soft light stays pixel-crisp.
technique.linework: Selective 1-art-pixel outline drawn outside the silhouette (sprite canvas grows by 1 px per side). Outline colour is derived from the neighbouring sprite pixel: on the shadow side (pixel to the left/top is solid) mix(colour*0.32, ink #150c29, 0.55); on the lit side mix(colour*0.55, plum #4a2c62, 0.45). Pixels flagged NOOUT get no outline; ghosts use outline alpha 0.55 and blue outline colours (#141640 / #3a4a9a). Never pure black.
technique.shading: Per-pixel Lambert-style shading: v = (n·L)*0.5 + 0.5 (+bias, +texture term) with L = normalize(-0.62, -0.5, 0.6) (upper-left, towards viewer), mapped to floor(v*rampLength) of an 8–14 step hue-shifted ramp. No smooth gradients inside sprites, only ramp steps; seams between two materials are broken with a 1-pixel checkerboard.
technique.lighting: Low warm sun from the upper left: rim #ffcfa2 (leaves #ffd08a) at 0.42 alpha (trees 0.5) on left edges, 0.75 strength on top edges; cool sky bounce #8d86ea at 0.22 on right edges. Shadows are the sprite silhouette sheared kx 0.8 / ky 0.3 towards the upper right, colour #1a1034, alpha bands 0.18/0.34/0.5. Emissive pixels (faces, eyes, gills, runes, lantern flame) skip rim and get additive banded glows (warm, amber, cyan, ice, pink, eye). Colour grade on screen: multiply gradient #fff0dc -> #f0dce0 -> #b8a6d4 -> #8a76c0 (left-top to right-bottom), screen-blended bloom, radial sun glow from the upper left, violet vignette #5c4a8a.
technique.texture: Posterised painterly ground: 3 octaves of tileable fbm quantised into 5 steps of the grass ramp, plus pixel blade tufts, blossom pixels in meadows, fallen leaves/petals in forest earth, brick-joint stone with moss. Leaf canopies use small Worley cells (4.6 x 3.6 px) each with a lit top row and dark seams.

paletteRules: Every material is a hand-picked ramp of 5–14 steps that hue-shifts: darks drift to blue/indigo/violet, lights drift to warm yellow-green or peach. Never darken by mixing with black.
The world is cool (teal-greens, violets, indigo); warmth comes only from light: rim light, pumpkin, flames, amber collectibles, sun grade.

Emissive colours (#fff6c4, #ffd05a, #ff9a2e for carved lantern faces; #ff4f7a for creature eyes; #7ee0cc/#d0fff2 for mushrooms and runes) are the only fully saturated light colours and always come with a glow.
Ground stays mid-to-dark (values of the grass ramp indices 3–8) so rim-lit sprites pop; ~55% grass, ~20% meadow/flowers, the rest forest earth, stone ruins, ponds.
Flowers are tiny 3–5 pixel motifs in pink, lavender, white, peach and gold with a #ffcf4e centre; they are sprinkled, never large.
Colours are finally multiplied by the peach-to-violet screen tint, so author sprites slightly brighter and warmer than they should look on screen.

typography.role: Body text, bar values, counters, card descriptions (pixel-grid sans that matches the art)
typography.css: font-family: 'Pixelify Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 15px; color: #ffe8c8; text-shadow: 0 1px 0 #1a0f24, 0 0 8px rgba(255,150,80,.5);

world.summary: An endless top-down forest clearing baked into 256x256-unit chunks at 1 px per unit: four materials (grass, forest earth, stone ruins, water) chosen per pixel from domain-warped fbm fields, each drawn from a 256x256 tileable pixel texture, with height-based edge shading (bluish cast shadows below taller materials, sunlit lips), decals and warm/cool light pools. Ground stays mid-to-dark so rim-lit sprites pop.
layers: Base fill #1e4a44 (ground colour while chunks build)
Material map per pixel from fbm fields (forest warped /760, meadow /520, ruins /600, water /420) with fine noise jitter and 1-px island despeckle; heights grass 3, stone 2, forest 1, water 0

Material textures: posterised grass (two variants), meadow grass with blossom-pixel map, forest earth with fallen leaves/petals/twigs and moss, brick-course cobbles (rows 12–20 px, stones 14–40 px) with cracks and moss joints, water ramp by depth with sky-reflection bands and ripple dashes Blossoms only show where the light-pool field is high, so they gather in drifts inside the sunlit pools instead of covering the meadow.

Edge pass: grass tips spilling over lower materials, cast shadow (factor 0.62, bluish) under higher neighbours above/left, dark lip on the lower edge, light sunlit lip on the upper edge, pale foam line at water edges
Macro light: dappled warm pools (r*1.17, g*1.07, b*0.95) and cool shade (r*0.9, g*0.93, b*1.06) from a /230 fbm field

Baked decals per 15-unit jittered cell: grass tufts, mixed flowers, lavender spikes, daisies, clover, pebbles, ferns, moss, lily pads, tiny glowing mushrooms; forest roots as pixel strokes; each decal has a 1-px shadow to the right

Per-frame ground overlay: additive flat light pools (main character 50 px warm + 16 px amber, lanterns, mushrooms, orbiting objects, projectiles) and 5-frame swaying grass/flower/fern sprites near the camera that lean away from the main character
Decals follow the light-pool field: flower beds and lavender stands in the sunlit pools, a tuft rim around them, only 5–6 % tufts on the open grass.

characters.summary: Characters are pixel sprites built in code from shaded primitives (ellipsoid blobs, cylinder-shaded capes, slanted 2-px legs, 2-px leaf strokes) on a 1-px grid, finished with the rim/outline pass and mirrored for left-facing. Every pose is its own drawn sprite: the main character (~18x31 px on a 28x34 canvas: ribbed pumpkin head rx 7.6 / ry 6.4 with an emissive carved face, teal hooded cape with a magenta lining, satchel, leather boots) is assembled from a pose record and cached per pose – an 8-pose walk, a breathing idle with blinks and glances, dash wind-up / stretch / skid, a hurt recoil, a throw and a cheer. The small violet root creature (26x36 canvas, two crown designs) hops, the translucent icy ghost (32x34) floats with a streaming tattered tail and peeling wisps, the large mossy colossus (64x62) stomps. Hits are drawn reaction poses with a short white flash, spawns rise from glowing spores, deaths dissolve into light.
rules: Head-heavy chibi proportions: head ~40% of the height, a short bell-shaped body, 2-px legs that slant from the hip to the foot so strides read.

Faces are emissive pixel patterns with a carved darker rim and a small additive glow; expressions are face variants, not effects: blink = dim 1-px slits, focus = slanted slits, hurt = squeezed '> <' eyes and an 'O' gasp, joy = '^ ^'.

Every creature type owns one ramp family and one glow colour: violet or magenta root creatures with pink-red eyes (#ff4f7a, core #ffe2ec), icy ghosts (#1a2252 … #f0fcff) with #bff4ff pupils, old-violet/ochre colossus with cyan eyes and rune (#6ff5e0).
Squash, stretch, lean and recoil are drawn into the pose (body radii, bob, shear, limb positions) – sprites are never scaled at runtime, so the art-pixel grid always holds.

Secondary motion lags one pose: the head lands a pose after the body, the satchel bounces with it, the stem leaf and leaf crowns flick against the movement, the cape hem trails (0–3 px) and the ghost's tail and arms trail its float.

Light always comes from the upper left: lit side via ramp + warm rim, right side via cool bounce; long shadows fall to the upper right with a contact ellipse (radius 6, large creature 14). A hopping creature's shadow loses its contact blob and slides along the light direction (h*0.8, -h*0.3).
Translucent figures (ghosts) use alpha ~230 at the head fading to ~90 in three tattered tail strands, a white-cyan rim #f4ffff and outline alpha 0.55 in blue (#141640 / #3a4a9a).
Mirror the unfinished pixels for the left-facing version and finish that again, so the warm rim always stays on the left.

props.summary: Scenery is painted with the same ramp shading, finish pass and long sheared shadow (kx 0.78, ky 0.28, alpha 0.3) as the characters: round oaks 104x106 with 30 leaf-cluster canopies, pink blossom trees, birches 70x112, mossy rocks, ruined pillars with ivy and optional cyan runes, stone arches 76x70, stone lanterns 16x31 with an emissive flame window, glowing mushroom clusters 26x22, berry/rose/white-flower bushes 30x21, lupines 16x26 and big ferns 30x18.
rules: Tree canopies are leaf clusters r 8–14 lit by the whole crown normal (0.42 - gx*0.24 - gy*0.3), with darker undersides and small leaf cells (4.6 x 3.6 px) each with a lit top row and a dark seam; trunks are cylinder-shaded bark with moss and spreading roots.
Trees use the leaf rim #ffd08a at 0.5 (cool bounce 0.26); everything else uses the standard rim #ffcfa2 at 0.42.
Stone props (pillars, arches, rocks, lanterns) use the stone ramp #141127 … #b3a2b0 with lit top rows, a lit left column, dark right/bottom edges, moss on tops and ivy climbing.
Emissive props carry their own light: stone lantern warm r16 at 0.6 with a ground pool r34 (flickering), mushrooms cyan r14 at 0.3 with a ground pool r30 (pulsing), runes cyan r12 at 0.4.
Props are anchored at their base and y-sorted with the characters; trees fade to 55% opacity when the main character walks behind them.
Only organic materials: bark, leaves, moss, weathered stone, flowers – no hard-surface or metal props.

effects.name: Additive banded glow
effects.how: Cached sprite per (colour, radius, flat): 3–5 concentric bands (r<5: 3, r<12: 4, else 5), colour ramp from hot core to tinted rim, alpha (1-band/bands)^1.6, band edges broken by Bayer dither; drawn with globalCompositeOperation 'lighter'. Flat variant (ry = 0.55r) is used for light pools on the ground.

effects.name: Seed projectile + ember trail
effects.how: 9x9 seed sprite in 16 rotations x 3 spin widths, amber glow r5 at 0.45, a 5-pixel trail behind it (#ffe9a0, #ffc35a, #ff9a4a, #f06a6a, #c04a8a, alpha 0.8-i*0.14) and a 2x1 ground shadow 7 px below.

effects.name: Impact
effects.how: Layered at the height of the struck body: a pink/ice/cyan bloom (0.16 s) as the core flash, a 7x7 four-point star (0.22 s), 3 3x3-pixel chips of the creature's own material (leaf/violet, ice, moss/ochre) thrown up with gravity 220, and 2 light motes that peel off sideways and rise for 0.4–0.6 s.

effects.name: Dissolve into light
effects.how: Drawn by the creature itself in 0.35 s: 14% white (#fff8f0) flash of its hit pose, then 6 baked dissolve frames – a noise front of 2-px clusters (top first; ghosts tail first) eats the body, a 1-px emissive seam runs ahead (pink #ffb4d0, ice, cyan #6ff5e0), the pixels behind it are tinted, and the freed pixels drift up 10–14 px as motes. The burst adds 8–26 petals from body height, rising motes, a bloom and a gold ring for the large creature. No gore.

effects.name: Spore emergence
effects.how: In 0.45 s: 6 glowing spores (10 cyan ones and 6 radiating ground seams for the large creature) spiral in from r 13–26 and lift, a soil mound (5 baked sizes, earth ramp with moss tips) swells, leaf tips poke out, then the creature bursts up in its stretch pose (clipped at the ground line), floats and lands in its squash pose. Ghosts gather from a rising column of ice motes and form head first (dissolve frames reversed), overshooting their float by 2 px.

effects.name: Collectibles
effects.how: Small amber shard 5x7 (shaded blob, emissive sparkle pixel, 2-frame twinkle) and large rose crystal 9x11 (faceted, 4 flat values by quadrant); both bob ±1.2 px with a flat glow under and a round glow on them; collecting releases a rising amber/rose mote, large ones add a ring.

effects.name: Orbiting lanterns
effects.how: 14x17 mini violet bulbs with a carved emissive face (#ffc040, #ff8a2a, #fff2b0) and a leaf on top, circling the main character with a warm glow r13 and a hot frame switching on sin(11t) > 0.2.

effects.name: Dash smear
effects.how: Two silhouettes of the stretch pose behind the main character – rose #ff86cc at alpha 0.42 (9 units back) and violet #9466f0 at 0.2 (18 units) – plus 5 dust puffs (three-lobed lilac clouds, ramp #5a4a7a … #e8dce6) and petals; the skid that follows kicks 3 more puffs off the planted heel.

effects.name: Gold ring burst
effects.how: Elliptical pixel rings (y squashed 0.62) in gold #ffe08e with an inner #c48a3a line, expanding to 80 and 44 px, plus 18 rising amber motes and 14 petals.

effects.name: Fireflies and drifting petals
effects.how: World overlay: 2 fireflies per 120-unit cell drifting on sines, a 1-px #f6ffd0 core with a 'fly' glow r5 pulsing via max(0, sin); 14 screen-wrapped petals blowing to the lower right.

atmosphere.summary: One low warm sun from the upper left/front (L = normalize(-0.62, -0.5, 0.6)) drives every rim and shadow; emissive objects add coloured additive light pools; the whole low-res buffer is then graded with tilt-shift strips, a peach-to-violet multiply tint, a squared 1/5-size bloom, an upper-left sun glow with god rays and a violet vignette before the integer upscale.
rules: Rim: empty left neighbour lerps to #ffcfa2 by 0.42, empty top 0.75 of that, empty top-left diagonal 0.3; otherwise empty right lerps to #8d86ea by 0.22 (0.4 strength if only diagonals are empty); emissive pixels skip it.
Shadows are the silhouette sheared kx 0.8 / ky 0.3 (props 0.78 / 0.28) towards the upper right, colour #1a1034, alpha bands 0.18 / 0.34 / 0.5, plus a contact ellipse under characters.
Coloured light: additive flat pools on the ground (warm r50 at 0.42 + amber r16 at 0.35 around the main character, lanterns r34, mushrooms cyan r30, projectiles r7), drawn with 'lighter'.
Tilt-shift: top and bottom 16% strips downsampled 2x, upsampled and masked back with a 0.95 -> 0 gradient.
Tint (multiply): linear gradient (0, 0.1H) -> (W, 0.9H): #fff0dc 0, #f0dce0 0.4, #b8a6d4 0.75, #8a76c0 1.
Bloom: downsample to 1/5, multiply the small image with itself twice so only highlights survive, draw back with 'screen' at alpha 0.7 with smoothing on.

Sun glow: radial gradient from (-0.05W, -0.1H), r 0.75W, rgba(255,170,110,.55) -> rgba(255,140,120,.22) at 0.35 -> 0, plus 7 soft god-ray bands (0.42 rad, alpha 0.05–0.12), drawn at 0.9 + 0.1 sin(0.35t).

Vignette (multiply, alpha 0.9): elliptical radial #ffffff at 0.22W -> #e4dcf0 -> #5c4a8a at 0.72W; deepen with a #4a3a8a multiply over time for a later hour; a full-screen #ff6a8a multiply flash when the main character is hit.

ui.summary: Storybook-at-dusk HUD: translucent deep-indigo panels (rgba(22,12,42,.72)) with thin gold #e8b85a borders, gold 45°-rotated diamond end caps, Cinzel engraved headlines with a warm glow and a 1–3 px dark drop line (#1a0f24), Pixelify Sans for numbers. Bars: a progress bar with a teal-to-cream fill (#3fb0ae -> #7ee0cc -> #ffd08a -> #fff2c4) and a teal glow, and a sunset-orange bar (#ffb36a -> #f07a3a -> #c2402c) next to a pixel heart icon. Cards are violet-to-navy gradient panels with a gold frame, a dark 4 px moat and a 5 px faint gold outer ring. Icons are 18x18 pixel sprites with the same rim/outline pass, scaled by integer factors.

motion: Pixel timing: poses are held and switched at 7–12 fps (on twos); only positions move every frame, always rounded to whole art pixels.

Main character walk: 8 poses at anim*1.3 (≈ 12 fps at walking speed) – contact, down, passing, up, mirrored. Body bob [0,1,0,-1,0,1,0,-1], near/far foot x ±3 with the lifted foot 1–2 px up on passing, the near arm counter-swings [-2,-1,0,1,2,1,0,-1] and the far arm swings opposite and 1.5x wider; the head and satchel use the previous pose's bob, the cape hem trails [0,1,2,1] px.

Idle: breathing bob 0/1 on a 1.3 s beat with the head 0.16 s behind, a blink every 3.1–4.4 s (0.12 s, some characters blink twice), the cape stirs for 0.5 s every 4.7 s, a glance back over the shoulder every 7.9 s; every actor gets a random phase offset.

Dash: 0.05 s wind-up crouch (bob 2, lean back, arms back, focused eyes) → stretch (stride ±4, lean +2, cape streaming 3 px, two afterimages) → skid for 0.14 s (heels dug in, lean -2, arms forward, cape swinging forward, dust) → settle.

Hurt: white flash for 67 ms, then the recoil pose (leaning back, head thrown back, arm flung up, squeezed eyes) with 1–3 px knock-back until ~170 ms; then an alpha 0.5 shimmer at 9 Hz while invulnerable. Throw: the near arm shoots straight forward for ~90 ms. Celebrate: both arms up, joyful eyes.

Small creature hop: 8 poses on 12 ticks [stand, stand, crouch, crouch, launch, rise, apex, apex, fall, land, land, recover] at anim*3.2 + seed*12 (≈ 1 hop per second): crouch squash 1 with the crown lifting, stretch -1 on launch, apex 5 px up, squash 1.3 on landing with the crown flopping. Hit: squashed recoil pose leaning 2 px back with the eyes squeezed, white for the first ~57 ms, 2 → 0 px knock-back over 130 ms.

Ghost: 8 float poses at 7 fps, lift 3 + [0,0,1,2,3,3,2,1] px (eased, holds at top and bottom); the tail stretches while rising and bunches while sinking, the arms trail by a pose, the mouth chews on poses 2–5, two wisps peel off the tail every 0.87 s. Hit: head thrown back, mouth wide, arms flung up, tail whipped forward, 3 px knock-back.

Large creature stomp: 8 poses on 12 ticks at anim*3.4 (holds on the weight and the lifted foot): the foot lifts 5 px, slams down, the body keeps sinking one pose later (by 3, squash rx +1.2 / ry -1.2), heaves up; arms swing against the legs, the crown lags, two dust puffs kick out at every contact. Hit: flinch pose (lean back, arms thrown up in front, eyes squeezed to a seam, maw open) with a 1-px recoil.
Light flicker: lanterns 0.82 + 0.12 sin(9t) + 0.06 sin(23t); main-character light pool 0.9 + 0.06 sin(7.3t) + 0.04 sin(17.1t); mushrooms pulse 0.75 + 0.25 sin(1.6t).
do: Render at 360 art pixels of height and upscale with an integer factor and smoothing off.
Shade every sprite pixel from the light vector (-0.62, -0.5, 0.6) into a hue-shifted ramp.
Run the finish pass on every sprite: warm rim left/top, cool bounce right, selective tinted outline.
Give every emissive pixel an additive banded glow and keep glows pixel-banded, not smooth.
Cast long sheared shadows to the upper right in #1a1034 with banded alpha.
Apply the grade (multiply tint, bloom, sun glow, vignette) on the low-res buffer, before upscaling.
Animate on twos with held, drawn poses: 8-pose walks with counter-swinging arms, hops with a crouch before and a squash after, one-pose lag on heads, leaves and capes, per-actor phase offsets.
Bake all sprites, shadows and ground chunks once; per frame only blit.
dont: Don't use pure black outlines or uniform outline colours.
Don't use smooth gradients, anti-aliased shapes or runtime sprite scaling – squash, stretch and recoil are drawn poses.
Don't light from the right or put shadows below/left — the sun is fixed at the upper left.
Don't draw at sub-pixel positions or rotate sprites freely (pre-bake rotations instead).
Don't use bright, saturated daylight greens or a flat unlit ground.
Don't let the UI become flat modern material design — keep gold trim, indigo glass and Cinzel.
Don't add glow to everything: emissives are rare focal accents (faces, eyes, mushrooms, lanterns, collectibles).
Don’t sprinkle flowers or tufts evenly over the whole meadow.
performance: Creatures (2 facings x 8 poses + hit pose + 6 dissolve frames, white flash copies made lazily), props, shadows, glows (cached by colour/radius), petals and digits are baked once at init (~150–350 ms). Main-character poses are assembled from a small pose record and cached per pose key the first time they appear (walk, throw, dash, hurt and the common idle poses are warmed at init; a pose's shadow is cached per leg/bob key). Ground chunks (256x256 px) are built incrementally via generators with a ~5 ms per-frame budget. Per frame: chunk blits, one sprite blit per actor (plus 2 tiny additive wisps per ghost, spores only while spawning), additive glows, ~50 sway sprites and the screen grade on the low-res buffer (one multiply, a 1/5-size bloom, two screen layers, vignette, tilt-shift strips) – cheap because the buffer is only ~640x360. Hot spots: many simultaneous glows and the full-buffer composites; keep glow radii small and counts bounded.
